title: Chain evaluations and triangle for opposite signed integral lines
statement: Let ℓ be prime, E a finite-dimensional field extension of ℚ_ℓ, and X a scheme. Let R be the completed integral coefficient sheaf on the small pro-etale site of X, L a locally free rank-one R-module sheaf, and e a family of opposite signed-power sheaf evaluation isomorphisms satisfying EvaluationFormula of [def-pur-integral-line-reduction-data]. For m an integer, let C_m be the functor on all unbounded cochain complexes sending P to the recorded total tensor P ⊗ power(L,m)[0]. There are natural chain isomorphisms a:C_m ⋙ C_{-m} ≅ Id and b:C_{-m} ⋙ C_m ≅ Id. In every degree and on every object of the site, a sends the total-tensor generator ((x⊗y)⊗z) to e(m)(y⊗z)•x, and b sends it to reverseEvaluation(e,m)(y⊗z)•x. They satisfy C_m(a_P inverse) followed by b_{C_m(P)} = identity for every unbounded cochain complex P. This statement concerns chain complexes only; it makes no assertion about derived tensor, localization comparisons, completeness or finite reduction.

proof.text: Compare the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor with the canonical monoidal tensor by tensorObjIsoSheafification and siteTensorRightIso. Naturality of the sheafification unit proves that this comparison takes the canonical pure tensor to siteSheafTensorTmul. Define the ordinary cancellation as reassociation, this comparison followed by the prescribed e, and the right unitor. The existing cancellation_pure calculation gives e(y tensor z) times x on every pure triple.

For a positive exponent, the signed-line theorem gives rank one. Its finite locally free cover supplies the covering-sieve hypothesis of the line inverse-pair theorem, by pulling each chart to every object in its generated sieve. Pure-tensor extensionality and EvaluationFormula identify the positive evaluation with functional evaluation, and the negative evaluation with braiding followed by that evaluation. Apply the existing tensor_triangles calculation. For a negative exponent package the first triangle as a tensor equivalence and use the first triangle of its symmetric equivalence. At exponent zero, pure-tensor extensionality identifies evaluation with the right unitor of the coefficient unit; monoidal coherence proves the triangle. In these three integer cases reverseEvaluation reduces to the indicated opposite evaluation.

Use the existing map₂HomologicalComplexFlipObjSingleIso to collapse each total tensor by a degree-zero line to termwise tensor. The inclusion of bidegree (i,0) followed by this collapse is tensor of the identity with singleObjXSelf.hom: unfold the single-summand projection and cancel the flip. Consequently the collapse sends coefficientTensorGenerator(x,y) to the canonical pure tensor (x,y). Whisker the two collapses and compose with mapHomologicalComplexCompIso of the ordinary cancellation and mapHomologicalComplexIdIso. Its action on a nested generator follows by applying the outer collapse, naturality of pure tensor under the inner collapse, and the ordinary cancellation formula.

Package the ordinary cancellations and the proved first triangle as an equivalence. Apply Equivalence.mapHomologicalComplex, then changeFunctor and changeInverse using the two collapse isomorphisms. Its inverse unit is the lifted first cancellation. Naturality of the first collapse identifies its counit with the lifted reversed cancellation. The functor_unit_comp triangle of this transported equivalence is exactly the required chain triangle. This is an identity of unbounded complexes, and no derived localization, flatness comparison, or representative hypothesis is needed.

theorem integral_line_chain_evaluations
    (L : scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E X) [L.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank 1]
    (e : Evaluations l E X L) (he : EvaluationFormula l E X L e) (m : ℤ) :
    ∃ (a : chainTensor l E X L m ⋙ chainTensor l E X L (-m) ≅ 𝟭 (Cx.{u, u} l E X none))
      (b : chainTensor l E X L (-m) ⋙ chainTensor l E X L m ≅ 𝟭 (Cx.{u, u} l E X none)),
      ChainEvaluationFormula l E X L m (-m) (e m) a ∧
      ChainEvaluationFormula l E X L (-m) m (reverseEvaluation l E X L e m) b ∧
      ∀ P : Cx.{u, u} l E X none,
        (chainTensor l E X L m).map (a.inv.app P) ≫
          b.hom.app ((chainTensor l E X L m).obj P) = 𝟙 _
